origin: hand-written from the published experimental local-server documentation; every value invented
notes: The shared pool is exhausted (usedRatio 1.0) and the rolling 5-hour window is almost exhausted, yet requests continue because Extra Usage is enabled and takes over. Amounts are integer cents with an explicit currency, so money arithmetic stays exact and the currency must be carried rather than assumed. monthlyChargeLimitEnabled with monthlyChargeLimitCents and monthlyUsedCents is the optional monthly spending cap, which is off by default; when the month's spend reaches the cap, Extra Usage consumption pauses for that month. The balance is personal-account-only and is shared across web, browser extension, desktop, mobile and Kimi Code, so it is ONE wallet and must not be counted per surface. Critically, spending this wallet does not change membership quota consumption or its refresh time - the two must stay separate rows with separate native units, and Extra Usage detail is a P1 concern. usages is keyed by window name and each entry carries usedRatio (a 0-1 float) plus an optional resetAt (RFC 3339). The window set is NOT fixed - the documentation says the client renders according to the entries actually delivered - so an absent window is Missing or Unsupported and must never be synthesized or defaulted to zero. usedRatio is a ratio: tokens must never be derived from it, and consumption is expressed in percentage points of the period allowance. resetAt values here carry an explicit +08:00 offset to show that the zone travels with the instant; the pool refreshes monthly by SUBSCRIPTION cycle, not by calendar month, so a refresh instant is not predictable from a payment date. monthTotal is the shared membership pool and is the only in-scope window. AMBIGUITY: the public documentation does not state whether usages is an object keyed by window name or an array of window objects; this corpus assumes the object form and the ambiguity is an open question for live reconciliation. Every JSON response from this server is wrapped in {code, msg, data, request_id} and the HTTP status is almost always 200, so the business result is code (0 = success) and must be checked before data. Some error envelopes carry non-empty data, which is why checking the status line or the presence of data first is wrong. request_id is an invented 26-character ULID-shaped string. The server binds plain HTTP on loopback (127.0.0.1:58627 by default) and requires a bearer token for every /api/* path except the liveness probe; that token belongs to another tool's runtime and must never be captured, stored or committed. The whole API is documented as experimental: endpoints, fields and event types may change in any version, so the /openapi.json served by the version actually in use has to be re-validated at runtime before any of these shapes is trusted.
